sql           - param-bound query (`:name` placeholders, no injection risk)
sql_dynamic   - text-substituted query (AI-generated SQL; see topic 'sql-dynamic')

api           - outbound HTTP (see topic 'sign' for auth). `with.method` defaults to GET, so set `method: POST` for a json/form body. The body is `json:` (a map or list, sent as JSON), `form:` (form-encoded), or `body:` (text sent as written; a map or list is sent as JSON; text written as a JSON document keeps each `${{ }}` value whole, JSON-escaped in a string and one JSON value elsewhere, so a request value cannot add keys). Outputs: status, headers, body (raw text) and json (when the response parses). `with.timeout:` caps the call (default 30s) - '570s'/'10m' or a bare number of seconds. A synchronous flow also ends at its own time limit (30 s by default, see time_limits), so pair a longer timeout with `on.request.timeout` or `mode: async`. `paginate:` reads every page of a list (api_paginate).
parallel      - run child steps at the same time (see parallel)

webhook       - outbound JSON POST: `with: { url, payload }`. `payload:` (a map or list; `body:` written as a map or list is the same) is the body, each `${{ }}` value resolved like an api `json:` value; `body:` as text is sent as written; with neither, the whole flow context without values derived from env (see the webhook gotcha below). Example and results: webhook.
email         - transactional email (see email_step, email_headers, email_attachments)
sms           - text message: `with: { to, body }` (see topic 'sms')
enqueue       - queue another flow of this app as a durable background job: `with: { flow, with, run_at?, unique_key? }` (see enqueue above)
compute       - server-side JS/TS function from static/ (see topic 'compute')
transcribe    - local audio → text (see topic 'transcribe')

inspect_private_upload - isolated server inspection of this app's private PDF/PNG; with: { source_path, kind: pdf|png } returns source_sha256 and PDF page geometry or PNG dimensions. It accepts no caller URL/path outside the selected app's private uploads and has a 90-second end-to-end deadline. Example: topic 'pdf' → signature_steps.

extract_text  - text of this app's private PDF, extracted in isolation (OCR optional); with: { source_path, record: {table, id}, ocr?: true|false (default true) }. Async/enqueued/scheduled flows only, never `transaction: true`. See topic 'pdf' -> extract_text.

render_pdf_signatures - isolated PDF stamping into a separate private output; with: { source_path, source_sha256, placements_json }. Each placement carries page, normalized displayed CropBox rectangle, private PNG signature_path and signature_sha256. Returns path, sha256, input_sha256 and page_count. It has a 120-second end-to-end deadline across private reads and parser work; a started storage save may take up to 30 seconds. Source files stay unchanged; output bytes are not promised deterministic, so the app must use durable job-completion CAS to choose one result and reconcile losing private artifacts. Example: topic 'pdf' → signature_steps.
delete_upload - delete this app's private upload: `with: { path, record? }` (see topic 'uploads' → private_deletion and deletion_example)
purge_current_user - erase the caller's account (see topic 'auth' → account_erasure)
revoke_user_sessions - end a user's sessions and tokens; only in the apply phase of an approved MCP command flow, refused in any other flow (see topic 'connector' → connector_commands)

broadcast     - send a server message to a WebSocket room's current members: `with: { room, payload }`. Members get `{type:'message', room, from:'server', payload}` (what bm.room() handlers already receive). See broadcast_step below. (The legacy flows.yaml `ws:` step is the old-format equivalent.)

notify        - in-app notification for one user: `with: { user_id, title, body?, link?, type? }`, stored, counted and announced live like a hooks.yaml `notify:` (only the recipient hears it), from any flow including cron. See notify_step below.

redirect      - 303 to `with.to`. A templated `to:` (any `${{ }}` / `:param`) must render a same-origin path (without a `\` in it) or a URL on this app's own host; an off-origin target is refused (step fails) unless its host is listed in `with.allow_hosts: [checkout.example.com]` (exact hostnames, list or comma string). A literal off-origin `to:` you wrote is allowed; javascript:/data:/vbscript:/file: never are. `benmore check` warns on a templated `to:` that is not pinned to a `/path` and has no allow_hosts. Example: redirect.

respond       - terminal response: `with: { status, json | body, content_type?, headers? }`. `status` may be a `${{ }}` that renders an integer 200-599. `content_type` and allowlisted `headers` are sent; see respond_headers below. On the hosted platform a 502, 504 or 520-530 status loses the body and the headers: Cloudflare replaces the response with its own text page (`error code: 502`), so answer 503 for an unavailable upstream and 500 for an unexpected failure. Push and benmore check warn on such a literal status and on a status expression that can answer one; see edge_error_status.

serve_file    - stream a file from uploads/ as the response. The FLOW is the auth gate, so it serves uploads/private/* to an anon caller it already authorized - no signed URL needed. with: { path, disposition: inline|attachment (or a `${{ }}` value/expression that resolves to one), filename? (may be a `${{ }}` template), expires_in? (literal signed-link lifetime for a private CDN file, 1s-6h; default 2m, 4h for audio/video), record? ({ table, id }: the row that owns a private file the caller did not upload; see api({at:'uploads'}) → private_ownership) }. See serve_file (keys and an example) and serving_private_files below.

proxy         - stream an outside service's answer (audio, image, video, PDF, CSV, ZIP) as the response: with: { url, method? (GET|POST), headers?, auth?, body | json, content_types (required), max_bytes?, timeout?, disposition?, filename?, cache_control? }. The scheme and host are literal text or an env value only; a public flow needs on.request.rate_limit. See proxy below.

if            - conditional branch. The key is `if:` (NOT `when:`: a step that uses `when:` is refused when the file is written and when the app loads). Forms: `if: ${{ steps.x.outputs.col }} == 'value'` (comparison), `if: ${{ gate.ok }}` (bare boolean - true/non-empty/non-zero is truthy), or an expression joining those with `&&`, `||`, `!` and parentheses (see `if:` conditions below). Wrap the gated steps under the if's `steps:`; `else:` holds the steps for a false condition (see else).
for_each / as - run steps once per element of a list (see for_each, loop_sources)
set           - assign named values for later steps: each `with:` key becomes `${{ key }}`
parse         - re-read the request body, JSON or form (see topic 'parse')
